Pan De Candelaria

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 8-10Prep 30 minCook 25 min

Pan De Candelaria is a traditional Mexican sweet bread enjoyed during Candlemas, also known as the Feast of the Presentation, celebrated on February 2nd. This festive bread is often shared among family and friends as part of the celebration marking the presentation of Jesus at the temple and the end of the Christmas season.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (480 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 2 1/4 tsp (1 packet) active dry yeast
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) warm milk (about 110°F/43°C)
  • 1/2 cup (115 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 3 large eggs
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • Zest of 1 orange
  • 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) warm water
  • 1 egg yolk (for egg wash)
  • 2 tbsp (25 g) sugar (for topping)

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, sugar, salt, ground cinnamon, and orange zest.
  3. Add the softened butter, eggs, vanilla extract, warm milk, and the activated yeast mixture to the dry ingredients.
  4. Mix all ingredients until a dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  6. Punch down the dough and shape it into a round loaf or several smaller loaves.
  7. Place the shaped dough on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  8. Brush the top with the egg yolk and sprinkle with sugar.
  9. Cover again and let rise for another 30 minutes.
  10. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  11. Bake the bread for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
  12. Remove from the oven and let cool on a wire rack before serving.

Tips

  • For a more festive look, you can shape the dough into a cross or other religious symbols before baking.
  • Serve Pan De Candelaria with hot chocolate or atole for a traditional Candlemas breakfast.
  • If you prefer, add a tablespoon of anise seeds to the dough for a licorice flavor common in some regional variations.
